record.paper_title: New results and open problems on subgraph centrality
record.original_question: Given a graph with n vertices, determine the largest possible number of interlacing values for subgraph centrality that a pair of its vertices can have. In particular, determine whether there are graph classes for which the upper bound d − 1 is attained, where d denotes the number of distinct eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix.

evidence.quote: Conversely, given a graph with n vertices, what is the largest number of possible interlacing values for a pair of its vertices? In particular, are there classes of graphs for which the bound d − 1 is attained?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let G be a simple undirected graph on n vertices with adjacency matrix A, and let A = sum_{k=1}^{d} mu_k E_k be its spectral decomposition, where mu_1 > mu_2 > ... > mu_d are the d distinct eigenvalues of A and E_k denotes the orthogonal projector onto the eigenspace of mu_k. For a vertex v of G, the subgraph centrality of v is defined as

   SC(v) = sum_{j>=0} (A^{2j})_{vv} / (2j)!  =  (e^A)_{vv}  =  sum_{k=1}^{d} (E_k)_{vv} cosh(sqrt(|mu_k|) * ... )  

equivalently SC(v) = sum_{k=1}^{d} (E_k)_{vv} e^{mu_k}. More generally one can consider, for a parameter t > 0, the quantity SC_t(v) = (e^{tA})_{vv} = sum_{k=1}^{d} (E_k)_{vv} e^{t mu_k}.

Given two vertices u, v of G, an "interlacing value" for the pair (u, v) is a positive real number t > 0 at which SC_t(u) = SC_t(v); equivalently, a positive zero of the function

   f_{u,v}(t) = sum_{k=1}^{d} ((E_k)_{uu} - (E_k)_{vv}) e^{t mu_k},

provided f_{u,v} is not identically zero. Since f_{u,v} is a real linear combination of d distinct exponentials, it has at most d - 1 positive zeros.

Questions:
(a) Determine, as a function of n, the maximum possible number of interlacing values that any pair (u, v) of vertices of an n-vertex graph G can have.
(b) Decide whether there exist classes of graphs in which the upper bound d - 1 is attained for some pair of vertices, and if so describe such classes.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem about the maximal number of interlacings of subgraph centralities between two vertices of a graph, and whether the natural upper bound d-1 (with d the number of distinct adjacency eigenvalues) can be attained. Web searches returned only general references on subgraph centrality and eigenvalue interlacing; no source resolving this specific extremal question was found, so it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Defines subgraph centrality as a weighted sum of closed walks expressible via the matrix exponential of the adjacency matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the standard definition of subgraph centrality used in the problem.
